explanation: Financial Regulation 107(m) states the Accountant-General shall “carry out revenue monitoring and accounting.”

text: Who issues officially approved forms bearing Treasury numbers for use in all federal ministries to ensure uniformity?
subject: Financial Regulations

text: What is the Accountant-General's role conceming the accounting policy of the federal government?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To implement policies set by the Minister of Finance.
To advise on the accounting policy.

explanation: Financial Regulation 107(0) states the Accountant-General shall "formulate the accounting policy of the federal government.”

text: Who is the officer responsible under the Constitution for the audit and report on the public accounts of the federation?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 108 identifies "the Auditor-General for the Federation” as this officer.

text: The Auditor-General's examination of accounts aims to ascertain whether:
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Public monies have been fully accounted for.
Monies have been expended for appropriated purposes.

explanation: Financial Regulation 108 lists all these as aspects the Auditor-General shall ascertain.

text: Which of the following is a statutory function of the Auditor-General?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 109(j) lists all these as statutory functions of the Auditor-General 150

text: The scope of work of the Auditor-General includes auditing the accounts of which entities?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Federal government establishments in states and FCT Area Councils.

explanation: Financial Regulation 109(i) lists all these as within the scope of the Auditor-General's work.

text: Who has free access to books of accounts, files, safes, security documents, and other records relating to government accounts?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Accountant-General and the Auditor-General or their representatives.
Accounting Officers and Heads of Finance.

explanation: Financial Regulation 110 states that “the Accountant General and the Auditor-General or their representatives shall, at all reasonable times, have free access to books of accounts, files, safes, security documents, and other records and information relating to the accounts."

text: What does the term "Accounting Officer” mean?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Any officer involved in financial transactions.
The Permanent Secretary of a ministry or head of an extra-ministerial office is responsible for human, material, and financial resources.
The Chief Executive Officer of a parastatal.
An officer who keeps a cash book.

explanation: Financial Regulation 111()) defines "Accounting Officer" as “the Permanent Secretary of a ministry or the head of extra-ministerial office and other arms of government who is in full control of, and is responsible for, human, material, and financial resources.” 151

text: An Accounting Officer is responsible for ensuring that any revenue collected is:
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Remitted to the appropriate authorities promptly and not spent.
Used to cover immediate operational expenses.

explanation: Financial Regulation 112(I)(1) states the Accounting Officer is responsible for “ensuring that any revenue collected is not spent but remitted to the appropriate authorities promptly.”

text: In compliance with the Public Procurement Act, Accounting Officers are charged with the responsibility of:
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Presiding over the activities of their Tenders Boards.
Ensuring adequate appropriation for procurements in their annual budget.
Integrating their entity's procurement expenditure into its yearly budget.

explanation: Financial Regulation 113 lists all these as special responsibilities of Accounting Officers under the Public Procurement Act.

text: If an Accounting Officer fails to comply with the provisions of the Public Procurement Act, who shall be held personally liable for any breach or contravention?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Only the subordinates who caused the breach.
The Accounting Officer, whether or not caused by them in person or their subordinates.

explanation: Financial Regulation 113(i) states the Accounting Officer "shall be personally liable for any breach or contravention thereof, whether or not such breach or contravention was caused by them in person, their subordinates, or any person to whom they may have delegated their responsibilities.”

text: The Head of Finance and Accounts is responsible for ensuring prompt rendition of which of the following returns?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 114(e) lists all these as retums for which the Head of Finance and Accounts is responsible for prompt rendition.

text: Question: What does the term "Sub-Accounting Officer” mean?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: An officer who prepares financial reports for the Accountant-General.
An officer entrusted with receipt, custody, and disbursement of public money, required to keep a cash book.
An officer who audits the accounts of a ministry.
The Head of Finance and Accounts.

explanation: Financial Regulation 115(1) defines "Sub-Accounting Officer” as "an officer who is entrusted with the receipt, custody, and disbursement of public money and who is required to keep one of the recognised Cash books."

text: Which of the following is NOT included in the definition of a "Sub-Accounting Officer"?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 115(ii) lists various officers included, but the "Minister" is the Political Head (FR 116), not a Sub-Accounting Officer.

text: If a directive from a Political Head results in unauthorized expenditure, who is responsible unless a report was made?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 117(ii) states, “the Accounting Officer shall be responsible for such an unauthorized expenditure unless a report had been made by the Accounting Officer to the Head of Service... or to the Minister."

text: What is the responsibility of the Political Head regarding his ministry, agency, and/or parastatal?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To supervise and control its activities.
To manage its day-to-day financial transactions.

explanation: Financial Regulation 118(i) states, “It shall be the responsibility of the Political Head to supervise and control the activities of his ministry, agency, and/or parastatal.”

text: "Revenue Collector” is defined as an officer who:
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Is entrusted with an official receipt, licence, or ticket booklet for regular revenue collection and keeps a cash book.
Only deals with large sums of money.

explanation: Financial Regulation 119 defines a "Revenue Collector” as "an officer, other than a Sub- Accounting officer, who is entrusted with an official receipt, license, or ticket booklet for the regular collection of some particular forms of revenue and who is required to keep a cash book.”

text: Who is an "Officer Controlling Expenditure"?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The officer to whom the control of a subhead or specified amount has been delegated by the appropriate Accounting Officer.
Any officer who signs payment vouchers.

explanation: Financial Regulation 121 defines an "Officer Controlling Expenditure” as “the officer to whom the control of a sub-head, or specified amount of a sub-head, has been delegated by the appropriate Accounting Officer.”

text: When a Ministry or Department is constituted as a Self Accounting Unit, who is charged with the installation and maintenance of a proper system of accounts for that unit?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Head of Finance and Accounts.

explanation: Financial Regulation 122 states that “the Accounting Officer as defined in Financial Regulation 111 is charged, in relation to that unit, with the installation and maintenance of a proper system of accounts.”

text: Which of the following is a general duty of public officers with monetary or financial responsibilities?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To ensure prompt collection of public revenue.
To promptly bring to account all moneys under proper Heads and Sub-heads.
To ensure proper provision for safekeeping of public moneys and documents.

explanation: Financial Regulation 123(j) lists all these as general duties.

text: Who is personally and peculiarly responsible for the due performance of the financial duties of their ministries and for any inaccuracies in accounts rendered under their authority?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Only the Head of Finance and Accounts.

explanation: Financial Regulation 124 states, "All officers are personally and peculiarly responsible for the due performance of the financial duties of their ministries/extra-ministerial offices and other arms of government.”

text: If an officer delegates or entrusts the performance of duties to a subordinate officer, is the delegating officer relieved of responsibility?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Only if the delegation is in writing.

explanation: Financial Regulation 125 states, "No officer shall be relieved of his responsibility should he delegate or entrust the performance of duties or any part thereof to his subordinate officer.”

text: Who is responsible for causing surprise inspections to be carried out on the accounts of officers with financial responsibilities?
subject: Financial Regulations

text: Who is responsible for ensuring the full collection of all government revenues and for promptly bringing them to account?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 201 explicitly states that Accounting Officers are responsible for the full collection of all revenues due to the government and for their prompt lodgment and accounting.

text: According to Financial Regulation 202, what must an officer receiving public money issue for every sum of money paid to the goverment?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 202 mandates that an official receipt shall be issued by the officer receiving public money for every sum paid to the government.

text: What information should an official receipt contain, as per Financial Regulation 204?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Only the amount of money received
The date, amount, and the name of the officer receiving it
The date, the name of the person paying, and a brief description of the transaction
The date, amount, and a brief description of the transaction

explanation: Financial Regulation 204 requires that official receipts must show the date, the amount received, and a brief description of the transaction for which payment is being made.

text: What type of receipt book is used by all Sub-Accounting Officers, unless a specially printed one or a receipt machine is used?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 206(i) specifies that General Receipts (Treasury Book 6) shall be used by all Sub-Accounting Officers for this purpose.

text: What is the process for making duplicate and triplicate copies of a receipt when using General Receipts (Treasury Book 6)?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: By using a special duplicating machine

explanation: Financial Regulation 206(ii) states that double-sided carbon paper shall be used to make the duplicate and triplicate copies of the receipt.

text: Who is responsible for giving the original receipt to the payer?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Head of Finance and Accounts
The officer who issued the receipt

explanation: Financial Regulation 206(ii) states that the original receipt shall be handed or delivered to the payer by the officer who issued the receipt.

text: What must a Revenue Collector do immediately upon receiving money?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Hand it over to the Sub-Accounting Officer
Enter the receipt in their cash book without delay
Issue a verbal receipt and collect a written one later
Keep the money in a safe until the end of the week

text: How often must a Revenue Collector make payments to a Sub-Accounting Officer?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: At least once a week, unless otherwise approved
Only when the amount is substantial

text: What document must support the payments made by a Revenue Collector to a ‘Sub-Accounting Officer?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: A Revenue Collector's paying-in Form (Treasury Form 15A)

explanation: Financial Regulation 209(i) states that the payments must be supported by a Revenue Collector's paying-in Form (Treasury Form 15A).

text: What must a Revenue Collector do with the official receipt they receive from the Sub-Accounting Officer?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Paste it in their cash book
Give it to the Accounting Officer

explanation: Financial Regulation 210 requires the Revenue Collector to paste this official receipt in their cash book on the payment side.

text: Who is responsible for ensuring that Revenue Collectors pay in their collections and produce their cash books for examination?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Head of Finance and Accounts
Sub-Accounting Officers and federal pay officers.

text: What is the maximum interval for a Revenue Collector's cash book to be produced for examination under normal circumstances?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 211 states that unless there are exceptional circumstances, the interval for examination shall not be greater than one month.

text: What kind of checks should the Accountant-General or Accounting Officer use to supplement routine checks on Revenue Collectors’ cash books?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Surprise inspections at the offices concerned

explanation: Financial Regulation 211 states that the Accountant-General or Accounting Officer shall supplement routine checks with surprise inspections at the offices.

text: Where must each ministry, extra-ministerial office, and other arms of government maintain a separate bank account for revenue?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: In a commercial bank of their choice
At the Central Bank of Nigeria or any other designated bank

options.text: To make transfers to the Consolidated Revenue Fund (CRF) account

subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To the Central Bank of Nigeria

text: What is the purpose of the Revenue Collector's Chart?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To track the daily activities of all staff
To record the number of receipts and licences in use
To give a continuous account of the value of receipts and licences
To serve as a monthly report of all expenditures

explanation: According to Financial Regulation 214(i), the chart is to give a continuous account of the value of receipts, licenses, and other revenue books issued for collections.

text: What should an officer who is neither a Revenue Collector nor a Sub-Accounting Officer do if they come into possession of public money?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Keep it safe until the end of the month
Lodge it without delay with a Sub-Accounting Officer
Hand it over to their Head of Department
Deposit it directly into the ministry's bank account

explanation: Financial Regulation 218 states that such an officer will lodge the money without delay with a Sub-Accounting Officer who will issue an official receipt.

text: What is the required procedure for a lodgement made by an officer who is neither a Revenue Collector nor a Sub-Accounting Officer?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: It must be accompanied by a hand-written note
It must be supported by a paying-in form (Treasury Form 15)
It must be entered in a private cash book

text: What happens if a Sub-Accounting Officer determines that an officer who has come into possession of public money is likely to do so again?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The officer is given a new job
The officer is given a promotion
The officer is supplied with an official receipt booklet
The officer is advised to open a private account for such funds

explanation: According to Financial Regulation 218, the Sub-Accounting Officer will arrange for the officer to be supplied with an official receipt booklet.

text: Who is responsible for checking Revenue Collectors’ cash books and cash balances at irregular intervals?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Head of Finance and Accounts

explanation: Financial Regulation 217 states that the Accounting Officer may consider it necessary for a revenue collecting office to have its cash books and cash balances checked at irregular intervals.

text: What must Accounting Officers do upon the establishment of any new revenue collecting office?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Notify the Head of Internal Audit
Notify the appropriate Sub Accounting Officer and the Auditor-General
Notify the Central Bank of Nigeria

text: What should be done with interest earned on bank accounts?
subject: Financial Regulations

It must be properly classified and paid to the Consolidated Revenue Fund.
It can be left in the bank account to accrue more interest.
It should be used to make up for any shortfalls in revenue.

subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Itis allowed with the Accounting Officer's approval.
It can be done if the amount is small.
Itis allowed as long as the Head of Accounts is notified.

text: What is the rule for Accounting Officers regarding the return of arrears of revenue?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: They must include only the arrears in respect of the headquarters.
They must include all arrears for which they are responsible to collect.
They should only return arrears that are substantial.
They are not responsible for retuming arrears.

subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The approval of the Accounting Officer.
The approval of the Head of Finance and Accounts.
The authority of the Minister of Finance.

An appropriate entry is made in the Paper Money Register.

To record the daily transactions of the Sub-Accounting Officer.
To track the movement of staff.

text: Who is responsible for ensuring that provisions for Value Added Tax (VAT) and Withholding Tax (WHT) are made and remitted?
subject: Financial Regulations

subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: They can delegate this responsibility to a junior staff member.
They are responsible for departmental control and collection.
They are only responsible for revenue received in cash.
They are not involved in revenue collection.

explanation: Financial Regulation 217 implies a departmental control over revenue collection, and the Sub-Accounting Officer plays a key role in this.

text: What is the process for correcting an error that has caused an apparent surplus in revenue?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The surplus must be immediately transferred to the Consolidated Revenue Fund.
The surplus can be withdrawn from the deposit to make good a subsequent deficiency, with specific approval.
The error cannot be corrected once the money is in the account.
The surplus can be used for departmental expenses.

Write off the arrears as irrecoverable.

text: Who must be notified of any amounts collectable by a department's officers?
subject: Financial Regulations

text: What is the role of the cashier in the process of handling cheques and other negotiable instruments received by post?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The cashier maintains the Paper Money Register.
The cashier enters the details in the Paper Money Register after it is opened by the Head of Accounts.
The cashier is not involved in this process.

text: What is the name of the form used by a Revenue Collector to pay in collections to a Sub-Accounting Officer?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 209(i) mentions the Revenue Collector's paying-in Form (Treasury Form 15A).

subject: Financial Regulations

text: When a Revenue Collector pays in his collections, what must he insert in the paying-in form (Treasury Form 15A)?
subject: Financial Regulations

The name of the receiving cashier [Correct Answer: B Explanation: Financial Regulation 209(i) states that the Revenue Collector will insert the Head and subhead to which the collections are to be credited.

text: What is the purpose of the Revenue Collector's paying-in Form (Treasury Form 15)?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To track the movements of the Revenue Collector.
To serve as an internal audit document.
To support the lodgement of moneys with a Sub-Accounting Officer.
To report a loss of funds. [Correct Answer: C Explanation: Financial Regulation 218 mentions that a lodgement with a Sub-Accounting Officer will be supported by a paying-in form (Treasury Form 15).

explanation: Financial Regulation 218 mentions that a lodgement with a Sub-Accounting Officer will be supported by a paying-in form (Treasury Form 15).

text: What is the role of the Head of Accounts in the process of handling cheques and bank drafts received through the post?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Opening the mail and maintaining the Paper Money Register.
Cross-checking the particulars of the original receipts with the details in the Paper Money Register.

Depositing the funds in the bank. [Correct Answer: B Explanation: Financial Regulation 233(ii) states that the Register shall be returned to the Head of Accounts, who will cross-check the particulars of the original receipts or licenses with the details entered in the Paper Money Register.

subject: Financial Regulations

text: What must the Revenue Collector's cash book entries include?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Only the amount of money received.
The dates and numbers of all receipts issued.
The name of the person who paid the money.

The signature of the receiving cashier. [Correct Answer: B Explanation: Financial Regulation 210 states that all receipt entries in the Revenue Collectors’ cash book shall include the dates and numbers of all receipts issued.

text: When is a Revenue Collector not relieved of their responsibility by delegation?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Only if the delegation is in writing.
According to Financial Regulation 125, the delegation of responsibility does not relieve the officer of their pecuniary responsibilities.
When the person delegated to is also a Revenue Collector.

text: How are the official receipts from a Revenue Collector's cash book to be numbered?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: In any order that is convenient.
In a random order to prevent fraud.

text: What is the name of the register used for incoming cheques and other negotiable instruments received by post?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 232(i) requires the use of a "Paper Money Register” for this purpose.

text: What is the purpose of the audit stamps that a Revenue Collector may be required to collect at the end of each duty?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To track the number of receipts issued.
To confirm the collection of revenue.
To verify the identity of the payer. D To serve as proof of payment.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1712, found in the index, describes the collection of audit stamps at the end of each duty, which are used to confirm the collection of revenue. 169

text: What are the primary instruments used to limit and arrange the disbursement of Federal Government funds?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 301 states: “The Annual Estimates and Appropriation Act are instruments used to limit and arrange the disbursement of the funds of the Federal Government.”

text: Who is responsible for any expenditure incurred without proper authority, as stated in Financial Regulation 301?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 301 clearly states that "Any officer controls a vote, or part thereof, who incurs expenditure without such authority does so on his sole responsibility and will consequently be held peculiarly responsible for his actions.”

text: From which fund is Recurrent Expenditure primarily paid?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 302(i) states: "Recurrent expenditure is paid from the Consolidated Revenue Fund..."

subject: Financial Regulations

When the Appropriation Act has not come into operation at the commencement of the financial year.

explanation: Financial Regulation 303 states: "A provisional General Warrant shall be issued where the Appropriation Act has not come into operation at the commencement of the financial year."

text: For how long can a Provisional General Warrant authorize the withdrawal of money from the fund?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 303 specifies "a period not exceeding six months.”

text: To whom is the original copy of a Provisional General Warrant addressed?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 303 states: "The original copy of a Provisional General Warrant is addressed to the Accountant-General with a signed copy forwarded to the Auditor-General."

text: What does the Annual General Warrant authorize the Accountant-General to do?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Only to pay for personal emoluments.
To issue funds to pay for personal emoluments and other services provided in the Annual Estimates.
To transfer funds from the Contingencies Fund.

text: Who may exclude an item of expenditure from the Annual General Warrant if special control is desired?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 304 states: “The Minister of Finance may exclude from the Annual General Warrant any item of expenditure over which it is desired to exercise special control."

text: A Supplementary General Warrant authorizes funds for additional services approved in which document?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 305 states: "A Supplementary General Warrant authorises the Accountant-General to issue funds to pay for the additional personal emoluments and other services which must have been approved in Supplementary Estimates..."

text: Under what circumstances may a Supplementary (Contingencies) Warrant be issued?
subject: Financial Regulations

subject: Financial Regulations

When additional provision is required under a sub-head and equivalent savings can be made under another sub-head of the same Head.
To authorize expenditure from the Contingencies Fund.
At the beginning of each financial year.

text: Virement from a Recurrent Expenditure Head of Account to a Capital Expenditure Head of Account is:
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Allowed with Minister of Finance approval.
Allowed only in the last quarter of the financial year.

explanation: Financial Regulation 316(iii) states: "Virement from one Head of Account in the Recurrent Expenditure estimates to another Head of account in Capital Expenditure estimates shall not be allowed and vice versa.”

text: Who must approve any variation in the Establishment or rates of allowances authorized for the Public Service?
subject: Financial Regulations

The Minister of Finance and the Office of the Head of Civil Service.

text: What is the purpose of a Supplementary (Statutory) Expenditure Warrant?

To authorize additional expenditure for votes chargeable against the Consolidated Revenue Fund by virtue of the Constitution.

subject: Financial Regulations
