options.text: Not later than the end of the financial year.
Not later than the first quarter of the Financial Year.
Not later than the tenth month of the budget year.
At any time during the financial year.

explanation: Financial Regulation 316(i) states: "Such application shall be made and approval obtained not later than first quarter of the Financial Year." 175

text: From which fund is Capital Expenditure paid?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 318 states: "Capital Expenditure is paid from the Development Fund..."

text: What is the maximum period a Provisional Development Fund General Warrant can authorize withdrawal of money?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 319 states: “for a period not exceeding six months.”

text: Who authorizes the withdrawal of money from the Development Fund through a Provisional Development Fund General Warrant?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 319 states: "the President shall authorise the withdrawal of money from the Development fund as may be necessary through the issuance of a Provisional Development Fund General Warrant..."

text: What is the purpose of a Development Fund Supplementary Warrant?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To fund new projects not in the estimates.
To accelerate the provision of funds formally allocated but not yet voted for a project.
To transfer funds between different economic program sections.

explanation: Financial Regulation 322(i) states its purpose is "to accelerate the provision of funds formally allocated but not yet voted for a project, by bringing forward an amount from the ‘Balance to Complete’ column of the Estimates.”

text: What is the limitation on the amount of funds brought forward by a Development Fund Supplementary Warrant?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: It can exceed the estimated total cost of the project.
It must not exceed the estimated total cost of the project as shown in the Annual or Supplementary Estimates.
It must be less than 50% of the project cost.

explanation: Financial Regulation 322(i) states: "the amount of the provision brought forward, when added to the total expenditure authorised for the current year, must not exceed the estimated total cost of the project as shown in the Annual or Supplementary Estimates.”

text: Who can authorize a Development Fund (Special) Warrant?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 323 states: "A Development Fund (Special) Warrant may be authorised by the Federal Executive Council (FEC)..."

text: What is the primary purpose of a Development Fund Virement Warrant?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To permit the issue of additional funds for the completion of a capital project where earlier funds were insufficient.
To transfer funds from the Consolidated Revenue Fund.
To authorize expenditure from the Contingencies Fund.

explanation: Financial Regulation 324 states: "The purpose of a Development Fund Virement Warrant is to permit the issue of additional funds required for the completion of a capital project, for which the funds earlier provided... was insufficient or inadequate..."

text: Which of the following is a limitation for a Development Fund Virement Warrant?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Re-allocation can be made between any Heads of Expenditure.
Funds can be provided for a new project.
Re-allocation may be made only within the same Head of Expenditure in the Capital Estimates.
It can increase provision to raise doubts about National Assembly intentions.

explanation: Financial Regulation 324(a) states: “re-allocation may be made only within the same Head of Expenditure in the Capital Estimates.”

text: Who issues a Development Fund Virement Warrant?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Minister of Finance after approval by the National Assembly.

explanation: Financial Regulation 324 states: "A Development Fund Virement Warrant shall be issued by the Minister of Finance after approval by the National Assembly."

text: The authority to incur expenditure from Public Funds other than the Consolidated Revenue Fund and Development Fund is what?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: A general directive from the President.
The appropriate warrant signed by the Minister of Finance, addressed to the Accountant-General.
A resolution from the Federal Executive Council.

explanation: Financial Regulation 326 states: "The authority to incur expenditure from any of the other Public Funds of the Government is the appropriate warrant signed by the Minister of Finance, addressed to the Accountant-General..."

text: What happens to an unspent balance on a recurrent expenditure vote at the end of the financial year?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Itis carried forward to the next year.
Itis transferred to the Development Fund.
Itis returned to the Federation Account.

explanation: Financial Regulation 314 states, "An unspent balance on a recurrent. expenditure vote cannot be revoted.” and FR 413(i) states “The authority for recurrent expenditure... lapses at the end of the financial year..."

text: If a Capital Expenditure amount conveyed by a warrant has not been cash-backed from the Consolidated Revenue Fund Account to the Central Capital Account (CCA) by year-end, what happens?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Itis transferred to the Contingencies Fund.
It requires re-appropriation by the National Assembly.

text: What happens to any balance in the Central Capital Account (CCA) at the end of the financial year that has not been cash-backed into the Capital Account of the spending Ministry/Agency?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: It lapses by March 31st of the following year.
Itis transferred back to the Consolidated Revenue Fund.
It is subject to a new appropriation.

explanation: Financial Regulation 413(ii)(b) states: "any balance in the CCA at the end of the Financial year which has not been cash-backed into the Capital Account of the spending Ministry/Agency shall lapse by 31st March of the following year."

text: If an amount is cash-backed into the account of a spending Ministry/Agency for capital expenditure, does it lapse?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Yes, at the end of the financial year.
Yes, by March 31st of the following year.
No, it shall be utilized for the purpose stated in the warrant.
Only if the project is completed.

explanation: Financial Regulation 413(ii)(c) states: "Any amount cash-backed into the Account of the spending Ministry/ Agency shall not lapse but shall be utilised for the purpose- stated in the warrant.”

text: Who is responsible for ensuring that expenditure is spread evenly over the year?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Officers controlling votes and officers acting under their instructions.
The Head of Finance and Accounts.

explanation: Financial Regulation 419 states: "Officers controlling votes and officers acting under their instructions shall arrange, r * far as it is practicable, to spread expenditure evenly over the year."

text: What is the primary responsibility of the Political Head of a Ministry regarding its activities?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To supervise and control its activities.

explanation: Financial Regulation 118(i) states: "It shall be the responsibility of the Political Head to supervise and control the activities of his ministry, agency and/or parastatal.”

text: What is the definition of a "Revenue Collector"?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: An officer entrusted with receipt, custody, and disbursement of public money.
An officer entrusted with an official receipt, licence, or ticket booklet for regular revenue collection and keeps a cash book.
An officer who approves revenue expenditure.

explanation: Financial Regulation 119 defines a "Revenue Collector” as “an officer, other than a Sub- Accounting officer, who is entrusted with an official receipt, licence or ticket booklet for the regular collection of some particular forms of revenue and who is required to keep a cash book.”

text: What is the definition of an "Imprest-holder"?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: An officer who manages the ministry's main bank account.
An officer entrusted with the disbursement of public money for which vouchers cannot be immediately presented to a Sub-Accounting Officer, and who keeps a cash book.
An officer who approves all capital expenditure.
An officer responsible for auditing revenue collections.

explanation: Financial Regulation 120 defines "Imprest-holder” as "an officer other than a Sub-Accounting officer who is entrusted with the disbursement of public money, for which vouchers cannot be presented immediately to a Sub-Accounting Officer and who is required to keep a cash book."

text: In a Self Accounting Unit, who is charged with the installation and maintenance of a proper system of accounts?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Head of Finance and Accounts.

explanation: Financial Regulation 122 states that "the Accounting Officer as defined in Financial Regulation 111 is charged, in relation to that unit, with the installation and maintenance of a proper system of accounts.”

text: What is the maximum number of days a public officer has to reply to formal queries or other enquiries from the Accountant-General and Auditor-General? A.7 days.
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 123(i)(p) states "within twenty-one days reply to formal queries or any other enquiries addressed to him by the Accountant-General and Auditor-General..."

text: Who is personally and peculiarly responsible for the due performance of the financial duties of their ministries and for any inaccuracies in accounts rendered under their authority?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Only the Head of Finance and Accounts.

text: Who is primarily responsible for making disbursements of public funds?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 401(i) states: "All disbursements of public funds shall be made by the Accountant General on the authority of the appropriate Warrant issued to him and also by Accounting Officers entrusted with the expenditure of public fund falling within the votes of charge of their ministries or extra ministerial offices and other arms. of government.”

text: Who retains the ultimate responsibility for the control of votes to the Federal Executive Council?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 401(ii) states: “the ultimate responsibility to the Federal Executive Council for the control of votes rests with the Account log Officers at all times."

text: What is the personal consequence for any officer making, allowing, or directing any disbursement without proper authority?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: They will be personally responsible for the amount involved
Their subordinates will be held responsible.
The expenditure will be absorbed by the Contingencies Fund

explanation: Financial Regulation 401(ii) states: "any officer making, allowing or directing any disbursement without proper authority shall be personally responsible for the amount involved."

text: What must a departmental vote book clearly show in respect of each sub-head?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The amount sanctioned in the Estimates.
Any additional provision by supplementary warrants.
Any reduction of the provision by virement.

explanation: Financial Regulation 402(i)(a) lists all these as details to be shown in the vote book.

text: How should any reduction of provision in a vote book by virement be indicated?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 402(i)(a)(iii) specifies: “Any such reduction should be shown in red ink."

text: What should be entered in the vote book in addition to expenditure incurred?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Both liabilities and commitments as soon as they are known or incurred.

explanation: Financial Regulation 403 states: "Similarly all liabilities and commitments will be entered as-soon as they are known or incurred.”

text: Who may delegate the day-to-day control of expenditure to a subordinate officer?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Head of Finance and Accounts.

explanation: Financial Regulation 404 states: "An Accounting Officer, at his discretion, may delegate the day-to-day control of expenditure to a subordinate officer..." 184

text: What document is issued by an Accounting Officer to authorize other officers to incur expenditure and sign vouchers on his behalf?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 405 states: "...he shall do so by issuing Authority to Incur Expenditure (A.LE)..."

text: What must accompany an Authority to Incur Expenditure (A.LE) issued by an Accounting Officer?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: A copy of the Annual Estimates.
A letter of approval from the Minister of Finance.

explanation: Financial Regulation 405 states: "...supported by appropriate cash backing..."

text: When an A LE. is issued to another ministry, what is the duty of the responsible officer in the receiving ministry?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To immediately spend all the funds.
To maintain a Vote Book and forward monthly returns of expenditure to the issuing Ministry.
To return the ALLE. to the issuing ministry.
To report directly to the Accountant-General.

explanation: Financial Regulation 406 states: “it will be the duty of the responsible officer in the receiving Ministry or Department to maintain a Vote Book and forward a monthly returns of expenditure to the issuing Ministry/ Department..." 185

text: What stamp must be affixed to all vouchers, indents, local purchase orders, job orders, and agreements when entered in the vote book?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 407 states: "...all vouchers, indents, local purchase orders, job orders, agreements shall be stamped ‘ENTERED IN VOTE BOOK' and initialed by the officer responsible for maintaining the vote book."

text: Who is responsible for ensuring that the requisite vote book entries are made before payments are authorized?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Head of Finance and Accounts.

explanation: Financial Regulation 407 states: "Officers empowered to incur expenditure must ensure by adding their initials against the. relevant entry that the requisite vote book entries are made before the payments are authorised by their signatures to the payment vouchers.”

text: How often does the Accountant-General furnish Accounting Officers with schedules of payments and adjustments?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: As soon as possible after the end of each month.

text: If a serious irregularity in a voucher is established or suspected, what is the first action the officer controlling the vote should take?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Report to the Minister of Finance.
Immediately investigate and report the circumstances.
Transfer the funds to a suspense account.

explanation: Financial Regulation 409 states: "Where a serious irregularity in a voucher is established or suspected the officer controlling the vote shall immediately investigate and report the circumstances..."

text: In the event of an unauthorized payment due to an incorrect certificate or entry on a voucher, who shall be held responsible and surcharged?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The certifying officer or the Sub-Accounting Officer.

explanation: Financial Regulation 409 states: "the certifying officer or the sub-accounting officer as provided under Regulation 420 shall be held responsible and surcharged for the amount involved.”

text: The signature of the officer controlling a vote on a voucher certifies the accuracy of what?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 410 states: “The signature of the officer controlling a vote, or an officer signing for him, certifies to the accuracy of every detail on the voucher.”

text: What is the minimum rank for officers authorized to sign payment vouchers?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Senior Executive Officer (Accounts) or Accountant I.

text: What must be attached to a voucher where a contract involves supplies of goods or work done?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: A certificate that payments are in accordance with contract terms.
A copy of the budget allocation.

explanation: Financial Regulation 412 states: "there will be attached to the voucher a certificate that the payments are in accordance with terms of the contract agreement..."

text: If a deduction is made from a contract payment for a penalty or fine, what happens to the deduction?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Itis credited to the appropriate revenue head.
Itis transferred to a suspense account.

explanation: Financial Regulation 412 states: “while the deduction shall be credited to the appropriate revenue head.”

text: When does the authority for recurrent expenditure conveyed by warrants lapse?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: At the end of the calendar year.
At the end of the financial year to which it relates.
When the funds are fully expended.

explanation: Financial Regulation 413(i) states: "The authority for recurrent expenditure conveyed by any of the warrants contained in Chapter 3 lapses at the end of the financial year to which it relates.”

text: For capital expenditure, what happens to any amount conveyed by warrants that has not been cash-backed from the Consolidated Revenue Fund Account to the Central Capital Account (CCA) by year-end?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Itis carried forward to the next year.
Itis transferred to the Development Fund.
It requires re-appropriation by the National Assembly.

text: What happens to any balance in the Central Capital Account (CCA) at the end of the financial year that has not been cash-backed into the Capital Account of the spending Ministry/Agency?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: It lapses by March 31st of the following year.
Itis transferred back to the Consolidated Revenue Fund.
It is subject to a new appropriation.

explanation: Financial Regulation 413(ii)(b) states: "any balance in the CCA at the end of the Financial year which has not been cash-backed into the Capital Account of the spending Ministry/Agency shall lapse by 31st March of the following year."

text: If an amount is cash-backed into the account of a spending Ministry/Agency for capital expenditure, does it lapse?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Yes, at the end of the financial year.
Yes, by March 31st of the following year.
No, it shall be utilized for the purpose stated in the warrant.
Only if the project is completed.

explanation: Financial Regulation 413(ii)(c) states: "Any amount cash-backed into the Account of the spending Ministry/ Agency shall not lapse but shall be utilised for the purpose- stated in the warrant.”

text: What is the rule regarding anticipated savings for payments?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: They can be utilized at any time.
They shall not be utilized for payments before they are due.
They can be transferred to a deposit account.

explanation: Financial Regulation 414 states: "Under no circumstances shall anticipated savings be utilised for' payments before they are due.”

text: How should expenditure be classified?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: According to the discretion of the Accounting Officer.
Strictly in accordance with the Estimates.
Based on the amount of the expenditure.

explanation: Financial Regulation 417 states: "Expenditure shall strictly be classified in accordance with the Estimates..."

text: What happens if expenditure is incorrectly charged to a vote?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: It will be adjusted in the next financial year.
It will be transferred to a general fund.
It will be reported to the Minister of Finance for approval.

explanation: Financial Regulation 417 states: "Expenditure incorrectly charged to a vote shall be disallowed.”

text: How should payments made on behalf of self-accounting units by Accounting Officers of other units be classified?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Directly to the expenditure sub-head of the Estimates.
To the appropriate Cash Transfer Account.

explanation: Financial Regulation 418 states: "shall be classified to the appropriate’ Cash Transfer Account and not-direct to the expenditure sub-head of the Estimates."

text: Who is solely liable for unauthorized expenditure in excess of the sum allocated?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Head of Finance and Accounts.

text: Before making any payment, what must a Sub-Accounting Officer satisfy himself about the voucher?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: That it is authorized by Warrant and correctly classified.
That the information furnished is correct and certificates completed.
That all deductions have been duly made.

explanation: Financial Regulation 420 lists all these as conditions a Sub-Accounting Officer must satisfy himself about

text: Who can effect an alteration to the classification of a voucher?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Head of Finance and Accounts.

explanation: Financial Regulation 421 states: "An alteration to the classification of a voucher shall only be effected by the officer controlling expenditure who will amend his Vote Book accordingly."

text: What is the responsibility of officers controlling votes regarding payment for services rendered?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To defer payments to the next financial year for budgetary reasons.
To ensure payments are settled within the financial year in which they were rendered.
To only pay for services after all claims have been perfectly validated.
To transfer all outstanding claims to a suspense account.

explanation: Financial Regulation 412(i) states: "Officers controlling votes are responsible for" ensuring that, as far as possible, payment for services rendered are settled within the financial year in which they were rendered.”

text: What must be entered into the Vote Book as liabilities?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: All instruments of commitments, indents, LPOs, job Orders, and signed contracts.

text: What happens if an officer neglects to press for claims from private parties, causing prejudice to the private party?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The private party is solely responsible.
The officer who neglected to press for claims shall be held responsible.
The claim will be written off.

explanation: Financial Regulation 412(i) states: "Neglect to do this will not prejudice the private party but the Officer who has neglected to press for claims shall be held responsible.”

text: What is the purpose of stamping vouchers "ENTERED IN VOTE BOOK"?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To confirm that the expenditure has been recorded as a commitment or payment in the vote book.
To show that the voucher has been audited.

explanation: Financial Regulation 407 implies this purpose, ensuring that financial commitments and payments are properly tracked against the allocated budget.

text: If a payment is made on account for a contract, what is the money claimed limited to?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The cost of the work certified to have been performed.
An arbitrary percentage of the contract.
The amount available in the vote.

explanation: Financial Regulation 412 states: “In the case o. payment on account, no money will be claimed other than the cost of the work certified to have been performed.”

text: What is the implication of an unexpended portion of any sub-head not being drawn for the purpose of setting it in reserve?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: It can be carried to a deposit account.
It can be placed in a suspense account.
It should not be drawn for setting in reserve or carried to a deposit/suspense account.

text: What is the rule regarding drawing unallocated stores for use?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: They can be drawn at any time.
They should not be drawn before they are required to utilize provision in the Estimates which would otherwise lapse.
They must be drawn by year-end.
They can be drawn to meet any unforeseen need.

explanation: Financial Regulation 414 states: "Un allocated stores may not be drawn for use before they are required in order to utilise provision in the Estimates which would otherwise lapse at the end of the financial year."

text: Who is responsible for providing the Internal checking section, intemal audit unit, and Paying Officer with specimen signatures of officers authorized to sign payment vouchers?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Head of Finance and Accounts.

explanation: Financial Regulation 411 states: "The Accounting Officer shall furnish the Internal checking section, intemal audit unit and the Paying Officer with the specimen signatures along with the list of relevant votes chargeable.”

text: If a discrepancy is found when examining schedules of payments and adjustments from the Accountant-General, what should be done?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: It should be ignored if minor.
It should be immediately brought to the notice of the Accountant-General.
It should be corrected by the Accounting Officer.
It should be reported to the Auditor-General only.

explanation: Financial Regulation 408 states: "Any discrepancy which such examinations may disclose should immediately be brought to the notice of the Accountant-General."

text: What is the definition of "Expenditure Classification"?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Categorizing expenses according to the Estimates.

explanation: Financial Regulation 417 implies that expenditure classification is the act of categorizing expenses according to the approved Estimates.

text: What is the primary purpose of the Departmental Vote Book?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To monitor and control expenditure against budget allocations.

explanation: Financial Regulation 402(i) clearly outlines the purpose of the vote book as monitoring expenditure against the Estimates.

text: What is the consequence if an officer controlling a vote incurs expenditure without proper authority?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The expenditure will be absorbed by the Ministry.
The officer will be held pecuniarily responsible for his actions.
The Accountant-General will rectify the error.
The Minister of Finance will issue a new warrant.

explanation: Financial Regulation 301 (which is referenced in 401) states: "Any officer controls a vote, or part thereof, who incurs expenditure without such authority does so on his sole responsibility and will consequently be held peculiarly responsible for his actions.”

text: When should liabilities and commitments be entered into the vote book?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: At the end of the financial year.
As soon as they are known or incurred.
Only when actual payment is made.

text: What is the role of the Sub-Accounting Officer regarding the classification of a voucher?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: They cannot change it arbitrarily; only the officer controlling expenditure can.
They are not involved in classification

explanation: Financial Regulation 421 states: “The classification of a voucher shall not be changed arbitrarily by a checking officer or Sub-Accounting Officer.”

text: Question: What is the primary objective of “Expenditure Control* as discussed in Chapter 4?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To ensure all allocated funds are spent.
To prevent fraud and waste in public spending.

explanation: The entire chapter emphasizes mechanisms (vote books, warrants, responsibilities) to ensure proper and authorized use of funds, directly aiming to prevent fraud, waste, and unauthorized expenditure. 195

text: Who has full authority to direct on all matters relating to the finance and accounting affairs of the federation, not assigned by law to any other Minister?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 501 states: "By the provisions of Sections 3 and 4 of the Finance (Control and Management) Act Cap 144 Laws of the Federation, 1990, the Minister of Finance shall have full authority to direct on all matters relating to the Finance and accounting affairs of the federation which are not by law assigned to any: other Minister."

text: What is the primary purpose of the Financial Regulations issued by the Minister of Finance?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To guide public officers on procurement only.
To guide public officers on the receipts and disbursements of Public Funds, and the management of public assets.

explanation: Financial Regulation 501 states: "Specifically, the Minister of Finance shall from time to time direct the issuance of the Financial Regulations to guide all public officers on the receipts and disbursements of Public Funds, as well as the management of public assets."

text: Who is responsible for issuing Treasury Circulars and Accounting Manuals to guide Accounting Officers and other employees?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Head of Finance and Accounts.

explanation: Financial Regulation 502 states: "Pursuant to FR 501, the Accountant-General shall issue from time to time Treasury Circulars and Accounting Manual to guide Accounting Officers and other employees of each ministries/extra- ministerial offices and other arms of government 01) all matters relating to the provisions of the Financial Regulations.”

text: What documents are federal ministries and other arms of government required to use for their daily financial transactions?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Financial Regulations, Treasury Accounting Manual, and Treasury Circulars issued by the Office of the Accountant General.

explanation: Financial Regulation 503 states: "For this purpose, federal ministries/extra ministerial offices and other arms of government shall use the Financial Regulations, Treasury Accounting Manual and Treasury Circulars issued by the Office of the Accountant General in accounting for their daily financial transactions.”

text: Who must approve any material variation of an existing accounting procedure or a proposed new accounting procedure?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Accountant-General after consultation with the Auditor-General.
The Head of Finance and Accounts.

explanation: Financial Regulation 504 states: "Any material variation of an existing accounting procedure, or a proposed accounting procedure to be introduced into a new office, must be approved by the Accountant-General after consultation with the Auditor-General."

text: Who must approve the purchase of accounting equipment or machines for a variation of an existing procedure, a new installation, or a major replacement?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Head of Finance and Accounts.

text: What document must be submitted to the Accountant-General when applying for a variation of an existing accounting procedure or introducing a new one?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 506 states: "A detailed flow chart shall be submitted to the Accountant General when application is being made for a variation of an existing procedure or introduction of a procedure to a new office.”

text: To whom should the approved Accounting Code, Internal Audit Guide, and Treasury Circulars be circulated within a ministry or self-accounting unit?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Only to the Head of Finance and Accounts.
To all officers within the ministry, extra-ministerial office and other arms of government for their guidance and compliance.
Only to the internal audit unit

explanation: Financial Regulation 507 states: "The approved Accounting Code and Internal Audit Guide of ministries/extra-ministerial offices and other arms of government or self accounting unit as well as Treasury circulars issued by the Accountant-General shall be circulated to all officers within the ministry, extra-ministerial office and other arms of government for their guidance and compliance.”

text: What is the relationship between an approved accounting code and the Financial Regulations if there is a conflict of detail?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 201 (which sets the precedent for accounting codes) states: "Where the approved code is at variance with these regulations, the code will prevail.” This principle is implied for all accounting codes.

text: Who is enjoined to acquaint themselves with these Regulations, the Finance (Control and Management) Act, and relevant Sections of the Constitution dealing with public finance?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: The Preface states: "Public Officers. are enjoined to acquaint themselves with these Regulations, the Finance (Control and Management) Act, Cap.144 Laws of the federation of Nigeria 1990, as well as the relevant Sections of the Constitution dealing with public finance. for proper guidance.”

text: What does the Finance (Control and Management) Act Cap 144 Laws of the Federation, 1990, regulate?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Certain financial matters of the government.
Only the salaries of public officers.

explanation: Financial Regulation 104 states: "Certain financial matters of government are regulated by the laws of the Federation enacted by the National Assembly. These include the Finance (Control and Management) Act CAP 144 Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 1990..."

text: Who is responsible for providing adequate accounting systems and controls in ministries and extra-ministerial offices?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Head of Finance and Accounts.

text: What is one of the duties of the Accountant-General regarding accounting codes and manuals?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To approve and ensure compliance with accounting codes, internal audit guides and stock verification manuals.
To formulate them without external input.
To distribute them to the public.

explanation: Financial Regulation 107(i) states: "approve and ensure compliance with accounting codes, internal audit guides and stock verification manuals of federal ministries, extra-ministerial offices and other arms of government.”

text: What type of audit ensures that laid down procedures are being observed in tendering, contracts, and store-keeping to prevent waste, pilferage, and extravagance?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 109(1)(c) states: "Financial Control Audit-to ensure that laid down procedures are being observed in tendering, contracts and store-keeping with a view to preventing waste, pilferage and Extravagance.”

text: Who has free access to books of accounts, files, safes, security documents, and other records relating to the accounts of all federal ministries?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Accountant-General and the Auditor-General or their representatives.
The Head of Finance and Accounts.

explanation: Financial Regulation 110 states: "By virtue of the responsibilities and functions of the Accountant General and the Auditor-General or their representatives shall, at all reasonable times, have free access to books of accounts, files, safes, security documents and other records and information relating to the accounts. of all federal ministries/extra ministerial offices and other arms of government. or units."

text: What is one of the key responsibilities of Accounting Officers under the Public Procurement Act?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To ensure adequate appropriation is available for Procurements in their annual budget.
To approve all payments without review.

explanation: Financial Regulation 113(b) states: "ensure that adequate appropriation is available for Procurements in their annual budget.”

text: What is the role of the Head of Finance and Accounts regarding compliance with Financial Regulations?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To ensure compliance by all staff under his control and supervision.
To approve all variations in accounting procedures.

explanation: Financial Regulation 114(a) states: “ensuring compliance with Financial Regulations and the Accounting Code by all staff under his control and supervision." Financial Regulations: Payments Procedure

text: All payment entries in the cash book/accounts must be vouched for on one of the prescribed treasury forms. In whose favor should vouchers be made out?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Head of Finance and Accounts.
The person or persons to whom the money is actually due.

text: Can a cheque be raised or cash paid for services for which a voucher has not been raised?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Only if the amount is small.

explanation: Financial Regulation 601 states: "Under no circumstances shall a cheque be raised or cash paid for services for which a voucher has not been raised.”

text: How should vouchers be raised for different sub-heads or different services?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: A single voucher can cover multiple sub-heads and services.
Separate vouchers shall be raised for separate sub-heads and different services.
Vouchers can be combined if the total amount is small.
Itis at the discretion of the Accounting Officer.

explanation: Financial Regulation 602 states: "Separate vouchers shall be raised for separate sub-heads. Separate vouchers shall also be raised for the payment of different services."

text: What kind of particulars should all vouchers contain?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Only the amount and payee name.
Full particulars such as dates, numbers, quantities, distances, and rates.
A brief description of the service.

explanation: Financial Regulation 603(i) states: "All vouchers shall contain full particulars of each service, such as dates, numbers, quantities, distances and rates, so as to enable them to be checked without reference to any other documents and will invariably be supported by relevant documents such as local purchase orders, invoices, special letters of authority, time sheets, etc.”

text: Which of the following is NOT an acceptable form of warrant authority to be quoted on vouchers for payments?
subject: Financial Regulations

text: What is strictly prohibited when preparing payment vouchers?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 604(a) states: "On no account shall vouchers be written in pencil."

text: What should be drawn immediately before and after the Naira (N) figure when it appears in words on a voucher?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 604(c) states: "A single thick horizontal line shall be drawn immediately before, and immediately after the Naira (N) figure where it appears in word."

text: Who is responsible for maintaining a payment voucher register and confirming the accuracy of entries before signing a voucher?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Head of Finance and Accounts.

explanation: Financial Regulation 605 states: "Officer controlling vote shall maintain a payment voucher register... Under no circumstances shall he sign a voucher until it has been entered in the register and has accordingly confirmed the accuracy of the entries therein."

text: Which copies of payment vouchers should be signed in full in ink or ball pens by the certifying officer and the payee?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Only the duplicate and triplicate copies.
Only the copy was sent to the Auditor-General.

text: Question: What is the rule regarding signing multiple certificates on a payment voucher?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Signatures can be written across multiple certificates.
Each certificate on a payment voucher shall be signed separately.
Only the first certificate needs a full signature.
A single signature at the bottom of the voucher is sufficient.

explanation: Financial Regulation 607 states: "Each certificate on a payment voucher shall be signed separately. Signatures shall not be written across one or more certificates.”

text: How should duplicate and triplicate copies of vouchers be marked?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: They do not need any special marking.
They should be clearly marked "Duplicate" and "Triplicate".
They should be marked "For Information Only".

explanation: Financial Regulation 608 states: "Duplicate and triplicate copies shall be clearly marked "Duplicate", "Triplicate" and copies shall not be accepted as payment vouchers.”

text: What is the maximum time a payment voucher should be held in the checking section?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 609(iii) states: "Payment vouchers received in the checking section must be promptly dealt with and under no circumstances shall a voucher be held in that unit for more than forty-eight (48) hours."

text: What is the procedure if an alteration to the amount of a voucher is necessary?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The alteration can be initiated by the certifying officer.
A new voucher must be prepared.
The alteration can be made and stamped "Corrected".
The Head of Finance and Accounts can approve the alteration.

explanation: Financial Regulation 610 states: "Alterations to the amount of a voucher whether in words or figure are not allowed. A new voucher must be prepared when necessary.” 204

text: When a voucher is submitted for payment at another station, how should it be sent after being checked and stamped?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Under the security schedule of Transfer of Payment Vouchers through the Sub-Treasurer.

explanation: Financial Regulation 612 states: "When a voucher is submitted to a Sub-Treasury or Cash Office for payment at another station, it will, after being checked and stamped in accordance with Regulation 609, be sent under security schedule of Transfer of Payment Vouchers through the Sub- Treasurer (See TF 193)."

text: Who is responsible for furnishing proof of identity if required when a payment is being claimed?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The ministry, extra-ministerial office, or other arms of Government authorising payment.

explanation: Financial Regulation 613 states: "...it is the duty of the ministry, extra-ministerial office and other arms of Government authorising payment to furnish proof of identity if required.”

text: When a payee is illiterate, whose mark must be witnessed by a literate official other than the paying officer?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 614 states: "Where a payee is an illiterate, his or her mark must be witnessed by a literate official other than the paying officer.” 205

text: How should payments to firms be made?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: By cheque crossed "Not Negotiable", "Account Payee only”, in favour of the firm.
By bank transfer directly to the firm's account.

explanation: Financial Regulation 616 states: "Payments to firms, shall be made only by cheques crossed "Not Negotiable", "Account Payee only", in favour of the firm."

text: What must be given on the face of the voucher, signed by the payee, when it is impracticable to obtain receipts for petty disbursements?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: . B. A certificate to that effect. C. An affidavit. D. A promissory note. Correct Answer: B Explanation: Financial Regulation 617 states: "When it is impracticable to obtain receipts for petty disbursements, a certificate to that effect must be given on the face of the voucher signed by the payee.”

text: If a payment to a firm is in doubt due to loss of relevant documents and an initial investigation reveals no prior payment, what must the payee issue to indemnify the federal government against double payment?
subject: Financial Regulations

text: Any payment due to or receipted by any government officer in his official capacity shall be paid to whom?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Head of Finance and Accounts.

explanation: Financial Regulation 619 states: "Any payment due to or receipted by any government officer in his official capacity shall be paid to the Treasury for which official receipt shall be obtained.”

text: What is the minimum amount for a receipt given for payment for goods supplied or services rendered to be liable to N50.00 Stamp Duty?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 620(a)(i) states: "Receipts given for payment for goods supplied or services rendered. If the amount is N1,000 or over a N50.00 stamp is required in respect of each signature acknowledging an amount."

text: Which of the following payments is NOT exempt from Stamp Duty under all conditions?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Payments for goods supplied or services rendered if the amount is N1,500.00.

explanation: Financial Regulation 620(b)(i) states that payments for goods supplied or services rendered are exempt if the amount is under N1,000.

text: Where banking facilities are available, all payments to the public other than firms covered under FR 514 must be made by cheque crossed in what manner?
subject: Financial Regulations

text: Immediately after payment is made, what should the paying officer stamp the original voucher and all copies, invoices, warrants, or other supporting documents with?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 622 states: “Immediately after payment is made, the paying officer shall stamp the original voucher and all copies, all invoices warrant or other supporting documents "PAID"."

text: If a payment voucher is presented to obtain cash for payment elsewhere (e.g., salaries), what form must accompany it?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 623 states: "Where a payment voucher is presented at a Sub-Treasury or Cash Officer for the purpose of obtaining cash for payment to be made elsewhere, as in the case of drawing. cash for the payment of salaries, wages, etc. It shall be accompanied by a cheque/cash order form signed by the officer authorising the voucher, and bearing the signature of the officer authorised to receive the cheque/cash.”

text: Vouchers withdrawn against cheque/cash order forms must be retumed to the Sub-Treasury or Cash Officer within how many days?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 624 states: "Vouchers withdrawn against cheque/cash order forms must be returned to the Sub-Treasury or Cash Officer within seven days.”

text: If a payment voucher is reported lost, and it is established that no loss or fraud has occurred, to whom should the Accounting Officer submit a report on the circumstances of the loss?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 630 states: "Where the Accounting Officer is satisfied that no loss or fraud has taken place he will submit a report On the circumstances of the loss of the voucher to the Accountant -General..." Financial Regulations: Bank Accounts and Cheques

text: Who is authorized to open an official bank account?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Director of Finance and Accounts.

explanation: Financial Regulation 701(i) states: "No official bank account shall be opened unless authorised by the Accountant-General.”

text: How many bank accounts is each establishment generally allowed to operate?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 701(ii) states: "Each establishment shall be allowed to operate only three (3) bank accounts as follows: (a) Salary Account; (b) Overhead Cost Account; and (c) Revenue Account.”

text: What is required for any bank account beyond the three specified types?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Approval from the Minister of Finance.
A resolution from the National Assembly.

explanation: Financial Regulation 701(ii) states: "No other bank account shall be allowed without the express approval of the Accountant-General."

text: How often should every organization submit a return of their bank accounts to the Accountant-General?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 701(v) states: "Every organisation shall submit a return of their bank accounts half yearly to the Accountant-General..."

text: Where should all Capital Accounts be maintained?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Central Bank of Nigeria or any other designated banks by the government.
A foreign bank for international transactions.
At the discretion of the Accounting Officer.

explanation: Financial Regulation 702 states: "All Capital Accounts shall be maintained at the Central Bank of Nigeria or any other Banks as may be designated by the government of the federation and authorised by the Accountant-General.”

text: Is the use of abbreviations allowed when writing the payee's name on a cheque?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: No, the name must be written in full.

explanation: Financial Regulation 703(iii) states: “The name of the payee shall be written in full and the use of abbreviation shall not be allowed.”

text: Who is responsible for fumishing certified specimen signatures of officers authorized to sign cheques drawn on official accounts?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Head of Finance and Accounts.

explanation: Financial Regulation 705(i) states: "All Accounting Officers shall furnish the details of commercial banks being used with certified specimen signatures of the officers authorised to sign cheques drawn on official accounts..."

text: What is the rule regarding delegation of authority to notify the bank of changes in authorized signatories?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: It can be delegated to a senior officer.
Delegation of this authority shall not be allowed.
It can be delegated with the Minister's approval.
Itis at the discretion of the Accounting Officer.

explanation: Financial Regulation 705(i) states: "Delegation of this authority shall not be allowed.”

text: What is the minimum rank for signatories to an official bank account?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Accountant | or designated officer of equivalent rank.

text: Under what circumstances should payment be made for services not yet performed or goods not yet supplied?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: In urgent cases with special approval.
If a mobilization fee is required.
Only if a contract is in place.

explanation: Financial Regulation 708 states: "On no account should payment be made for services not yet performed or for goods not yet supplied."

text: Who has the right of access to records of all bank accounts of all ministries, extra-ministerial offices, and other arms of government?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Accountant-General and the Auditor-General or their representatives.
The Head of Finance and Accounts.

explanation: Financial Regulation 709 states: “The Accountant-General and the Auditor-General or their representatives shall have the right of access to records of all bank accounts of all ministries, extra ministerial offices and other arms of government..."

text: What happens if a government bank account is overdrawn?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The bank will automatically cover the overdraft.
The officer responsible shall be made to refund any bank charges incurred thereon.
Areport is sent to the Minister of Finance.

explanation: Financial Regulation 710 states: “In the event of an account being overdrawn, the officer responsible shall be made to refund any bank charges incurred thereon.”

text: Can idle funds in the accounts of missions abroad be invested in short-term deposits?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Yes, but only with the prior approval of the Accountant-General.
Yes, at the discretion of the Head of Mission.
Only if the amount is substantial.

explanation: Financial Regulation 711(i) states: "Idle funds in the accounts of missions abroad may be invested in short term deposits but with the prior approval of the Accountant- General.” 212

text: What is the implication if an officer pays public money into a private bank account?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The officer is deemed to have done so with fraudulent intention.
The money will be transferred back to the government account.

explanation: Financial Regulation 713 states: "An officer who pays public money into a private account is deemed to have done so with fraudulent intention."

text: Where a bank account is kept, what type of payments should generally be made by cheques?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 714 states: "Where a Bank account is kept, only sufficient cash to meet small payments shall be allowed while all payments should be made by cheques.”

text: How often must officers authorized to keep bank accounts compare entries in bank statements with their cash books?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Weekly and at the close of each month.

explanation: Financial Regulation 716 states: "All officers authorised to keep bank accounts must compare on- weekly basis, and at the close of each month, the entries appearing in the bank statements with those in their cash books..." 213

text: Who should sign every request for official cheque books?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: One of the authorized signatories to the account and countersigned by the Head of Accounts.

explanation: Financial Regulation 718 states: "Every request for official cheques books shall be signed by one of the authorised signatories to the account and countersigned by the Head of Accounts.”

text: When a cheque is received, how should it be made payable?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 719(i) states: "A cheque received should be made payable to "Federal Government of Nigeria."

text: What is the maximum amount for a cheque that must be properly confirmed with designated banks before acceptance?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 719(i)(h) states: "All cheques above N20, 000 must be properly confirmed with the designated banks before acceptance.”

text: Can cheques received by a Sub-Accounting Officer be endorsed or assigned to a third party?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Yes, if the third party is another govemment entity.

explanation: Financial Regulation 720(i) states: "On no account may cheques received by a Sub-Accounting Officer be endorsed or assigned to a third party."

text: What is the processing period for cash transfers in respect of AIEs issued by ministries/extra-ministerial offices in favor of state offices, in view of the electronic banking system?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 721(i)(c) states: "the processing period of cash transfers in respect of AlE's issued by ministries/extra ministerial offices and other arms of government in favour of state offices shall not exceed Seven (7) working days.”

text: Who is ultimately responsible for ensuring the recovery of dishonored cheques?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The officer who accepted the cheque.

explanation: Financial Regulation 730(i) states: “It shall be the ultimate responsibility of the Accounting Officer concerned to ensure that these amounts are recovered, instituting legal action if necessary.”

text: Can a dishonored cheque be held as cash?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Yes, with the Accounting Officer's approval.
Only if the amount is small.

explanation: Financial Regulation 732(ii) states: "Under no circumstances may a dishonoured cheque be held as cash."

text: What is the primary purpose of maintaining a departmental dishonored cheques register?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To ensure clearances are pursued and recoveries affected.
To record all incoming and outgoing cheques.
To provide a summary of daily bank transactions

explanation: Financial Regulation 733(ii) states: "The register shall be checked monthly by the Head of accounts to ensure that clearances are pursued and recoveries effected.” Part 2: Financial Regulations: Cash Book and Monthly Accounts

text: Who is required to keep a Treasury Cash Book No. 153A or an approved cash book?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Head of Finance and Accounts.

explanation: Financial Regulation 801 states: "A Sub-Accounting Officer as defined by FR 115 is required to keep a Treasury Cash Book No.153A (see Appendix 9) or a cash book in such form as may be approved by the Accountant-General, in consultation with the Auditor-General."

text: How are receipt and payment vouchers numbered for entry into the cash book?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: According to the type of service.

explanation: Financial Regulation 802 states: "Receipt and payment vouchers shall be numbered consecutively, from NO.1 each month in the order in which the amounts are received or paid, and will be entered into the cash book accordingly.”

text: What do the terms "Revenue" and "Expenditure" refer to in the context of Chapter 8?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Receipts and payments under Heads in the recurrent and capital Estimates.
All financial transactions of the government.
Only income and outgoings from special funds.

explanation: Financial Regulation 803 states: “The terms "Revenue" and "Expenditure" refer to receipts and payments, respectively under Heads appearing in the recurrent and capital Estimates..."

text: What does "Below-the-line" refer to in Chapter 8?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Receipts and payments for services specified in the approved Annual Budget estimates.
Receipts and payments for services not specified in the approved Annual Budget estimates.
Funds that are not subject to audit.

explanation: Financial Regulation 803 states: "...while Below-the-line refers to receipts and payments for services that are not specified in the approved Annual Budget estimates.”

text: What should be done with cheques held as cash at the close of business?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Paid to the bank or cleared on the next business day.

explanation: Financial Regulation 804 states: "Cheques held as cash at the close of business will be paid to the bank or otherwise cleared on the next business day.”

text: Can a cheque that has been presented to the bank and returned unpaid be held as cash?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Yes, with the Accounting Officer's approval.
Only if the amount is small.

explanation: Financial Regulation 804 states: "In no circumstances may a cheque which has been presented to the bank and returned unpaid be held as cash.”

text: Who signs the cash book at the end of each month to certify the correctness of entries and cash balance?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 805 states: "The cash book shall be signed at the end of each month by the Sub Accounting Officer whose signature will be taken as certifying the correctness of the entries and cash balance.”

text: How should unpresented cheques that become stale after 6 months be handled?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Written back in the Cash Book after written confirmation of non-payment from the bank.
Reported as a loss of funds.

explanation: Financial Regulation 807(a) states: "Unpresented cheques which become stale after 6 months should be written back in the Cash Book after written confirmation of non-payment from the bank."

text: How often should Sub-Accounting Officers submit their accounts?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: By the seventh day of the following month.
By the fourteenth day of the following month.
By the end of the following month.

explanation: Financial Regulation 808(i) states: "Sub-Accounting Officers shall submit their accounts by the fourteenth day of the following month or within such other period as may be prescribed by the Accountant-General."

text: What is the Monthly Consolidated Account also known as?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 809 states: "The Monthly Consolidated Account otherwise known as "Transcripts" will consist of..."

text: What information should a voucher substitute contain?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Month and year of account, payment voucher number, classification, amount paid, and sufficient details to permit identification of the transaction.
The reason for the missing voucher.

explanation: Financial Regulation 810 states: "Voucher substitutes will show month and year of account and will also contain payment voucher number, classification, amount paid and sufficient details to permit identification of the transaction.”

text: What register must a Sub-Accounting Officer maintain for outstanding vouchers?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: A register of outstanding vouchers (Treasury Form 73).

explanation: Financial Regulation 811(i) states: "Sub-Accounting Officer shall maintain a register of outstanding vouchers (Treasury Form 73) which shall be marked off 11S they are received.”

text: Who is personally responsible for obtaining acquittal for payments out of public funds until the relevant payment vouchers are obtained?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 811(ii) states: “It is the personal responsibility of the Sub-Accounting Officer to obtain acquittal for the payments out of public funds and this responsibility exists until he has obtained the relevant payment vouchers (See Regulation 621)." 220

text: What is the purpose of reconciling outstanding items in the Bank Reconciliation Statement expeditiously?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To ensure the effectiveness of the statement.

explanation: Financial Regulation 807(c) states: "Prompt action should always be taken to obtain bank advice to confirm the various entries in the bank statement as the effectiveness of the Bank Reconciliation Statement lies in the prompt clearance of outstanding items."

text: What kind of payments are Revenue and Expenditure vouchers submitted in duplicate to Sub-Accounting Officers?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: All types of payments unless otherwise directed by the Accountant-General.

explanation: Financial Regulation 803 states: "Revenue Expenditure, and Below-the-line vouchers will be submitted to Sub-Accounting Officers in duplicate, except as May be otherwise directed from time to time by the Accountant- General." 221

text: Question: What is the primary purpose of adjustments in financial accounting, as described in Chapter 9?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To increase or decrease cash on hand.
To make transfers between accounts without actual cash receipt or payment.
To record daily petty cash transactions.
To prepare annual financial statements for audit.

explanation: Financial Regulation 901 states: "Adjustments are effected by means of Journal entries which enable transfers to be made from one account to another without actual receipt or payment of cash.”

text: Which of the following is an example of a transaction that would typically be handled through an adjustment?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Payment for a new office supply order.
Correction of accounting errors arising from misclassifications.
Receipt of monthly revenue from a government agency.

explanation: Financial Regulation 901 lists "correction of accounting errors arising from misclassifications” as an example of an adjustment.

text: Which Treasury Form (TF) is primarily used for inter-ministerial transactions?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 903(i) states: "The Adjustment Voucher (TF 23) which is designed to adjust inter-ministerial transactions is mostly used in - ministries, extra-ministerial offices and other arms of government.”

text: How many copies of the Adjustment Voucher (TF 23) are typically submitted?
subject: Financial Regulations

text: In the Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation (OAGF), what type of journal voucher is used for adjustments and transfers made before the "Below-the-line Statement" is extracted?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 904(i) states: "...the SN and PJV are used in the Office of the Accountant General of the Federation (OAGF) for the Preparation of Consolidated accounts, While SNs are used for all adjustments and transfers that are made before the “Below the-line Statement” is extracted...”

text: For what primary reason are Principal Journal Vouchers (PJVs) prepared in the OAGF?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To adjust differences between ministry transcripts and bank statements.
To correct misclassification of accounts detected by the main accounts.
To reclassify accounts before the Trial Balance is prepared.

explanation: Financial Regulation 904(ii)(a) states that PJVs are prepared “to correct misclassification of accounts detected by the main accounts.”

text: What information must an adjustment voucher clearly indicate?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Only the amount of the adjustment.
The reason for the adjustment and full reference to the original debit or credit.
The name of the officer who prepared the voucher.
The date of the next audit.

explanation: Financial Regulation 905 states: "Adjustment vouchers must clearly indicate the reason for the adjustment, and must make full reference to the original debit or credit being adjusted...”

text: Adjustments in which Unallocated Stores and Workshops Accounts are credited must be embodied in which document?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 907 states: "Adjustments in which Unallocated Stores and Workshops Accounts are credited must be embodied in the relevant Material Expense Statement (M.E~S.)."

text: If an adjustment voucher supports an adjustment between votes that is not to be included in the Material Expense Statement (M.E.S.), whose signature must it bear?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The engineer or officer actually in charge of the vote.

explanation: Financial Regulation 907 states: "Vouchers supporting adjustments between votes which are not to be included in the M.E.S. must bear the signature of the engineer or officer actually in charge of the vote."

text: Where should vouchers in respect of adjustments arising from reconciliations be submitted?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To the Accountant-General only. CC. Wherever possible, they should accompany the Reconciliation Statements.
They should be filed separately and not submitted.

explanation: Financial Regulation 908 states: "Vouchers in respect of adjustments arising from reconciliations should, wherever possible, accompany the Reconciliation Statements.

text: What types of transfers are effected by Principal Journal Vouchers (PJVs) at the end of the month?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Transfers related to revenue collection only.

explanation: Financial Regulation 904(ii)(c) states that PJVs are prepared to "effect month-end transfer of accounts from Above-the-line Accounts to Below-the-line Accounts.”

text: What is the purpose of Supplementary Journal Vouchers (SJVs) in the OAGF?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To adjust differences between ministry transcripts and bank transfer statements, and to re-classify accounts before the Trial Balance.
To correct misclassifications and effect annual transfers.
To record all incoming and outgoing cash.

explanation: Financial Regulation 904(iii) states SJVs are prepared "to adjust differences between ministry transcript's figures and those contained in the Bank Transfer Statements prepared by the Sub- Treasurer of the Federation; and to re-classify accounts before the Trial Balance is prepared.”

text: When an adjustment voucher is accepted by a ministry, extra-ministerial office, or other arm of government, what is returned as evidence of acceptance or rejection?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: A copy of the original memo.
One of the fully signed adjustment vouchers.

explanation: Financial Regulation 903(iii) states: “The ministry, extra-ministerial office or other ams of government which is receiving the adjustment voucher shall stamp and return one of the fully signed vouchers as evidence of acceptance or rejection.” Financial Regulations: Imprests

text: Who is authorized to issue Imprests?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Accountant-General of the Federation and Accounting Officers of Self-Accounting ministries/extra-ministerial offices.
The Head of Civil Service of the Federation.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1002 states that “"Imprests are issued by the Accountant-General of the Federation and the Accounting Officers of Self Accounting ministries/extra-ministerial offices and other arms of government.”

text: What document conveys the authority for issuing Imprests?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The General Imprest Warrant issued by the Minister of Finance to the Accountant-General.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1002 specifies that "The authority for issuing Imprests is conveyed in the Annual General imprest Warrant issued by the Minister of Finance to the Accountant-General (see Appendix 5).

text: When is the General Imprest Warrant issued by the Minister of Finance?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: At the beginning of each calendar year.
Immediately after the enactment of the Annual Appropriation Act.
Only when a special imprest is required.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1003(i) states: "The General Imprest Warrant shall be issued by the Minister of Finance immediately after the enactment of the Annual Appropriation Act.” 226

text: Which type of imprest can be replenished from time to time during a financial year?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 1004(i)(a) describes Standing Imprests as those "which may be replenished from time to time during a financial year by the submission of paid vouchers to ‘Sub-Accounting Officers for reimbursement.”

text: When must a Special Imprest be retired in full?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: At the end of the financial year.
Immediately the purpose for which it was granted has been achieved.
When the imprest holder is transferred.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1004(i)(b) states that Special Imprests "must be retired in full when the purpose has been achieved.”

text: What is explicitly prohibited regarding the use of personal advances in disguise of Special Imprest?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Using them in the procurement of stores.
Using them for minor office repairs.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1004(ii) explicitly states: "On no account shall personal advance be used in disguise of Special Imprest, in the procurement of stores which is governed by the provision of chapter 23 of these Regulations."

text: What Treasury Form (TF) is used for the issue and payments of impress?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 1006 states: "Authorities for issue-and payments of imprests shall be effected on a Departmental Imprests Warrant (Treasury Form 9)..."

text: Where should all imprests issued and their retirement be recorded?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 1006 specifies: "All imprests issued and their retirement shall be recorded in a special imprest ledger.”

text: How should issues of imprest be classified in the General Ledger Account?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To "Expenditure" in the name of the Imprest Holder.
To "Revenue" in the name of the Imprest Holder.
To "Imprests” in the name and designation of the Imprest Holder.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1006 states: "Issues shall be classified to "Imprests" General Ledger Account in the name and designation of the Imprest Holder.”

text: How often should replenishment of amounts paid from an imprest be effected?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Only at the end of the financial year.
As needed, without a fixed schedule.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1010() specifies: "Replenishment of amount paid from imprest will be effected at least once a month.”

text: When must all standing imprests be retired?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: On or before 31st December of the financial year in which they are issued.
Within one month of the issue date.
When the imprest holder goes on leave.
Only upon the explicit instruction of the Accountant-General

explanation: Financial Regulation 1011(i) states: "All standing imprests must be retired on or before the 31st December of the financial year in which they are issued..."

text: If an imprest is retired at a station other than where the warrant was drawn, who must the imprest holder immediately notify?
