It should be held indefinitely by the government.
It shall not be paid without the authority of the Accounting Officer.
It must be used to pay off their debts.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1511 states that any balance of salary or other money due to an officer who has been convicted or dismissed for misappropriation or theft shall not be paid without the Accounting Officer's authority.

text: How long does the Sub-Accounting Officer have to pay unclaimed salaries, allowances, and pensions to the Treasury?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: At the end of the financial year.
As soon as the cash is withdrawn.

text: What two documents are required to be issued when an officer is transferred from one ministry to another?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: A Last Pay Certificate and a certified true copy of the Personal Emolument Records.
A letter of recommendation and a transfer letter.
An updated curriculum vitae and a new contract.
A bank statement and a new Treasury Form 14.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1514(i) requires that a Last Pay Certificate along with a certified true copy of the Personal Emolument Records shall be issued when an officer is transferred.

text: What information must the Last Pay Certificate and Personal Emolument Record show?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The last pay date, details of deductions, and the balance recoverable.

explanation: According to Financial Regulation 1514(ii), the last pay certificate and personal emolument record must show the last pay date, full details of deductions, and the balance recoverable.

text: What must a paying officer do with the total of each type of deduction from emoluments?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Transfer it to a suspense account.
Enter it as a receipt in his cash book.
Ignore it for the final payment calculation.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1515 states that the paying officer shall enter the total of each type of deduction from emoluments as a receipt in his cash book.

text: What must the gross amount of emoluments be charged against?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The relative personal emoluments sub-head of the current year's estimates.

text: Who must approve the procedure and method for the recording and calculation of personal emoluments?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 1517 mandates that the procedure and method for recording and calculating personal emoluments must be approved by the Accountant-General

text: Which of the following is not a record required for the standard payroll system under FR 1518?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Pay Statement to be issued to the individual officer.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1518(i) lists the Personal Emoluments Record, payroll, and Pay Statement as part of the standard payroll system, but makes no mention of a birth certificate.

text: What is a key duty of the officer controlling expenditure as per FR 1519?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To personally approve every single salary payment.
To ensure the standard personal emoluments records are kept securely.
To ensure the records show the officer's standard rate of pay, incremental date, allowances, and deductions.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1519 details the information that the officer controlling expenditure must ensure is shown in the standard personal emoluments records, including rate of pay, incremental date, and deductions

text: What is the purpose of the completed personal emolument form according to FR 15212
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To serve as the basis for opening the group registers, which must be audited before an officer is included in the payroll.
To justify the officer's annual leave.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1521(ii) states that the completed personal emolument form shall be the basis for opening the group registers, which must be audited before any officer is included in the payroll.

text: What must the salary section be informed of in writing at the earliest possible time?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Any variation that may affect the salary of any officer.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1522(i) requires that the salary section must be informed in writing of any variation that may affect an officer's salary at the earliest possible time.

text: Who should not be the officer directly in charge of preparation of the payroll, according to FR 1523(ii)?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: An officer not below the rank of Senior Accountant.
The officer directly in charge of variation control.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1523(ii) specifies that the officer directly in charge of variation control must not be the officer directly in charge of preparation of the payroll and must work independently.

text: What should cheques for cash payments be drawn in the name of, according to FR 15267
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The bank manager. B.The Accounting Officer or head of the field headquarters office in the state.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1526(d) states that for cash payments, cheques should be drawn in the name of the Accounting Officer or head of the field headquarters office in the state

text: What must be sought and secured for cash in-transit?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 1527(i) states that the assistance of police escort must be sought and secured for cash in-transit

text: How are salary payments for part of a month calculated on retirement or termination of appointment?
subject: Financial Regulations

text: What is the role of the Accounting Officer concerning personal emolument records?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To ignore them. B.To ensure they are maintained to prevent over-payments and ensure correct deductions are made.
To only maintain them for senior staff.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1506(ii) states that the Accounting Officer shall ensure personal emolument records are maintained to ensure payments are made when due, that over-payments are not made, and that all required deductions are made

text: Who should be promptly informed of any variation or contingency likely to affect an officer's salary, such as death or dismissal?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 1507(i) states that the officer controlling expenditure shall promptly be informed of any variation or contingency likely to affect officers’ salary..

text: What is the purpose of a summary payment voucher in payroll preparation?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To list all the officers in a department.
To capture the total basic salaries, allowances, deductions, and net amount payable for all officers in a pay-point.
To request a loan for an officer.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1524(d) states that a summary payment voucher shall be raised to capture the total basic salaries and allowances, total deductions, and the net amount payable for all officers in a pay-Point.

text: What does Financial Regulation 1601 primarily define? A, The responsibilities of an Auditor-General.
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The role of an Accounting Officer in a self-accounting unit.
Procedures for revenue collection. D Guidelines for capital expenditure.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1601 explicitly defines the "Role in a self-accounting unit" for an Accounting Officer

text: Who approves the grant of self-accounting status to a Ministry, Extra-Ministerial Office, or other arms of government?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 1602 states that the Accountant-General's approval is required for self-accounting status

text: What is one of the key responsibilities of the Accounting Officer in a self-accounting unit, as per Financial Regulation 1603(a)?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To personally conduct all internal audits.
To ensure strict observance of existing financial rules and regulations.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1603(a) mandates that the Accounting Officer shall ensure strict observance of existing financial rules and regulations governing the receipt and disbursement of public funds.

text: What is the Accounting Officer responsible for regarding the preparation and defense of annual budget proposals?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Personal compilation and defense under their supervision.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1603(i) states that the Accounting Officer is responsible for compiling and defending the annual budget proposals under his supervision.

text: What kind of statements must the Accounting Officer ensure are produced monthly and quarterly, according to FR 1603(j)?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 1603(j) requires monthly and quarterly statements of budget performance to be produced by the Accounting Officer.

text: Who is responsible for ensuring the adequacy of internal control over revenue collection, as per FR 1603(g)?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 1603(g) assigns the responsibility for adequate internal control over revenue collection to the Accounting Officer.

text: What type of balance must the Accounting Officer ensure is included in the monthly accounts (FR 1603(vii))?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 1603(vii) requires the Accounting Officer to ensure the closing cash/bank balance is included.

text: What is the role of the Accountant-General in relation to the accounting instructions issued by the Accounting Officer, according to FR 1603(h)?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To provide specific directives to embrace the general provisions of Financial Regulations.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1603(h) mentions that specific directives from the Minister of Finance or the Accountant-General should be embraced in the detailed accounting instructions.

text: What is the fundamental principle regarding public funds in a self-accounting unit, as implied by Chapter 16?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: They can be used for personal expenses.
They must be managed with strict adherence to financial regulations.
They are to be invested without oversight.

explanation: The entire chapter emphasizes the Accounting Officer's responsibility to ensure strict observance of financial rules and regulations governing public funds.

text: What is a core element of proper financial management in a self-accounting unit that the Accounting Officer must ensure?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Transparency and accountability in financial operations.

explanation: The regulations emphasize strict observance of rules, proper accounting, and budget performance reporting, all pointing to transparency and accountability.

text: What happens if an Accounting Officer in a self-accounting unit fails to comply with the Financial Regulations?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: They may face disciplinary action and surcharges.
Their unit loses self-accounting status automatically.

explanation: While not explicitly detailed in the provided Chapter 16 snippet, financial regulations generally impose disciplinary actions and surcharges for non-compliance. The emphasis on "strict observance" 26 implies consequences for failure.

text: What is the primary objective of monthly and quarterly statements of budget performance?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To monitor financial progress and ensure adherence to approved budgets.
To prepare for external audits only.

explanation: These statements are crucial for monitoring financial performance against the budget.

text: What type of control is emphasized for the collection of all revenues under the responsibility of the Accounting Officer?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 1603(g) specifically highlights an "adequate system of Internal control".

text: What is the general rule regarding the disbursement of public funds in a self-accounting unit?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Funds can be disbursed at the discretion of the Head of Department.
Disbursements must strictly follow existing financial rules and regulations.
Funds can be transferred to private accounts.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1603(a) states the need for strict observance of existing financial rules and regulations governing the disbursement of public funds.

text: What should detailed accounting instructions issued by the Accounting Officer embrace?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Only the Accounting Officer's personal preferences.
The general provisions of Financial Regulations and specific directives from higher authorities.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1603(h) specifies that detailed accounting instructions should embrace general provisions of Financial Regulations and directives from the Minister of Finance or the Accountant-General. 269

text: What action is crucial for newly established revenue collecting offices regarding notification?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: They must notify the local police.
They must notify the appropriate Sub Accounting Officer and the Auditor-General.
They must notify the general public.

explanation: Financial Regulation 217 (from a related section but relevant to accounting officer duties) states Accounting Officers will notify the appropriate Sub Accounting Officer and the Auditor-General of the establishment of any new revenue collecting office

text: Who primarily bears the responsibility for any discrepancies in financial records within a self-accounting unit?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: The Accounting Officer is charged with ensuring strict observance of regulations and proper accounting, implying ultimate responsibility for discrepancies

text: What is the frequency for producing accounts to the Accounting Officer to show cumulative yearly totals of expenditure and revenue?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 1603(f) states that monthly accounts are produced to the Accounting Officer to show cumulative yearly totals. 270

text: What is specifically forbidden in handling money received in the course of official duties by an officer who is not a Revenue Collector or Sub-Accounting Officer?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Lodging them with a Sub-Accounting Officer.
Supporting lodgement with a paying-in form.

explanation: Financial Regulation 218 states that such monies must be lodged "without delay".

text: What happens to interest eared on bank accounts, according to Financial Regulations?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: It can be retained by the unit.
It must be properly classified to the appropriate revenue head and paid to the Consolidated Revenue Fund.
It can be used for departmental welfare.
It is transferred to a suspense account.

explanation: Financial Regulation 222 (from a related chapter but a general principle) states that interest eamed on bank accounts must be properly classified and paid to the Consolidated Revenue Fund.

text: What is the rule about making deductions from revenue collections to adjust a previous over-credit?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 223 explicitly states, "No deductions shall be made from any revenue collections or other receipts to adjust a previous over-credit".

text: What is the implication of the Accounting Officer ensuring payments are made when due and that over-payments are not made?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: They are only concerned with timely payments.
They are responsible for the accuracy and timeliness of payments.
They only focus on preventing fraud.

explanation: This responsibility encompasses both the punctuality and correctness of payments, indicating a dual focus on timeliness and accuracy.

text: What type of reporting must the Accounting Officer ensure is accurate for management and control purposes?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Comprehensive financial reports including budget performance.

explanation: The Accounting Officer is responsible for budget proposals, defense, and monthly/quarterly budget performance statements, all indicating comprehensive financial reporting. 272

text: What is the overall policy of intemal audit according to Financial Regulation 1701?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To replace external auditors. B To provide a complete and continuous audit of accounts and records of revenue, expenditure, plant, and stores.
To focus only on revenue generation.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1701 states the policy is to provide a complete and continuous audit of the accounts and records of revenue, expenditure, plant, and stores.

text: Who is responsible for the appointment of the Internal Auditor?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 1702 specifies that the Accountant-General shall be responsible for the appointment and deployment of Internal Auditors.

text: What is a key duty of the Intemal Auditor as per Financial Regulation 1703?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To conduct an annual audit of the entire Ministry.
To audit and certify all payment vouchers.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1703(d) lists one of the duties as auditing and certifying all payment vouchers.

text: According to Financial Regulation 1704, what must the Head of the Internal Audit Unit prepare annually?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: A list of staff to be promoted.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1704 requires the Head of the Internal Audit Unit to prepare an annual audit program. 273

text: What is the Internal Auditor's guide for auditing procedures known as, according to FR 1708?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 1708 states that the Head of Internal Audit Unit shall prepare and issue an "Audit Guide" for the use of audit staff.

text: Which of the following is a restriction on the duties of audit staff, as per FR 1709?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: They cannot make suggestions for improvements.
They are not allowed to handle cash or stores.
They must not report their findings.
They are not allowed to communicate with other staff.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1709(a) prohibits audit staff from handling cash, receipts, stamps, or stores.

text: What must an Internal Auditor do when he discovers an apparent abuse of Financial Regulations?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Report it immediately to the Accountant-General.
Call the attention of the appropriate officer in writing.
Take disciplinary action against the officer.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1703(a) states the Internal Auditor shall call the attention of the appropriate officer in writing where there is any apparent abuse of Financial Regulations.

text: What is required for the issuance of audit stamps to Internal Audit staff?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Verbal permission from the Head of Department.
A form signed by the Accountant-General.
A requisition form (Treasury Form 65A) in triplicate.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1711 details the procedure for issuing audit stamps, requiring a requisition form (Treasury Form 65A) in triplicate.

text: What must an Internal Auditor do with audit stamps at the end of each duty?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Keep them for the next day's work.
Account for and return them to the Head of the Internal Audit Unit.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1712 states that Internal Auditors must account for and return their audit stamps to the Head of the Internal Audit Unit at the close of each day's duty.

text: What is strictly prohibited regarding audit stamps?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Transferring them to another staff member.
Collecting them from the Head of the Internal Audit Unit.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1713 states that "Audit stamps are not transferable” and must not be used by anyone other than the officer to whom they were issued.

text: What is the primary purpose of the Internal Audit Unit?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To perform administrative tasks for the department.
To provide an independent appraisal of accounting, financial, and other controls.
To sign off on all procurement contracts.
To manage the department's human resources.

explanation: The policy of internal audit and its duties, as described in Chapter 17, are centered on providing an independent appraisal of financial and other controls to the Accounting Officer.

text: To whom does the Internal Auditor submit periodic audit reports?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 1706 explicitly states that periodic audit reports are submitted to the Accounting Officer.

text: What is the relationship between the Internal Auditor and the staff whose accounts they are auditing?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Internal Auditor is superior to the staff.
The Internal Auditor is subordinate to the staff.
The Internal Auditor should be independent of the staff.
The Internal Auditor works under the supervision of the staff.

explanation: The entire purpose of internal audit is to provide an independent appraisal, which implies independence from the staff whose work is being audited.

text: What type of register must be maintained by the Head of the Internal Audit Unit?
subject: Financial Regulations

text: What is a key function of the Head of the Internal Audit Unit concerning the audit program?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To delegate all tasks to junior staff.
To amend the program as he deems fit, without approval.
To ensure the audit program is effectively carried out.
To present the program to the general public.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1704 mandates that the Head of the Internal Audit Unit shall “ensure that the programme is effectively carried out.”

text: What does the "management letter" from the Internal Auditor primarily address?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Irregularities and failures of intemal control.

explanation: The management letter is used to communicate discoveries of negligent disregard of financial regulations or abuse of internal controls.

text: In addition to auditing payment vouchers, what other type of vouchers does the Internal Auditor audit and certify?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 1703(d) states that the Internal Auditor's duties include auditing and certifying "all payment and revenue vouchers." Part 2: Financial Regulation: Board of Survey: Cash and Stamps

text: According to Financial Regulation 1801, what is the primary purpose of an Annual Board of Survey?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To inspect the condition of government vehicles. C.To physically inspect, count, and verify the cash, stamps, and other security documents held by Accounting Officers.
To review the annual budget proposal.

text: Who is responsible for convening the Annual Board of Survey for a Ministry, Extra-Ministerial Office, or other arm of government?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Head of the Internal Audit Unit.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1802 specifies that the Accounting Officer is responsible for convening the Annual Board of Survey.

text: What is the minimum number of members on a Board of Survey, according to FR 1802?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 1802 states that the Board shall consist of at least three members.

text: What must the members of the Board of Survey be, as a requirement for their appointment?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: They must be from the same department as the officer being surveyed.
They must be from different departments or units.
They must be senior accounting officers.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1802 requires that the members shall be from different departments or units other than the one whose accounts are being surveyed.

text: What is the duty of the Board of Survey conceming the cash, stamps, and other security documents?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To sell them at a public auction.
To physically count and verify them against the relevant accounting records and registers.
To destroy them if they are found to be old.

text: Who must be present during the physical count and verification of cash, stamps, and other security documents by the Board of Survey?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The officer-in-charge of the items being surveyed.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1803 requires that the officer-in-charge of the cash, stamps, or other security documents must be present throughout the physical count and verification.

text: What must the Board do with any surplus or shortage of cash discovered during the survey?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Keep the surplus and ignore the shortage.
Report the matter immediately to the Accounting Officer for prompt investigation.
Adjust the books to reflect the new balance.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1807 mandates that any surplus or shortage must be reported immediately to the Accounting Officer for prompt investigation.

text: When should the business of the office being surveyed be suspended?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Throughout the period of the physical inspection.
At the beginning and end of the financial year.
Only if a shortage is discovered.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1806 states that the business of the office or unit shall be suspended for the duration of the physical inspection.

text: What type of report must the Board of Survey prepare and submit?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: A verbal report to the Accounting Officer.
A report in triplicate, which must be signed by all members.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1807 states that the Board of Survey shall prepare a report in triplicate, signed by all members. 279

text: What is the purpose of a "surprise" Board of Survey?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To give notice to the officer-in-charge. 8 To check for discrepancies without prior warning.
To only be conducted when there is a known shortage.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1804 allows for the convening of "surprise" Boards of Survey to check cash, stamps, and other security documents without prior warming.

text: What action should be taken if an Accounting Officer in a field headquarters office is absent when a surprise Board of Survey is convened?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The survey must be postponed until the officer returns.
The survey can proceed without them.
The next most senior officer shall act in his place.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1804 states that if the Accounting Officer is absent, the next most senior officer shall be required to act in his place for the purposes of the survey.

text: What is the responsibility of the members of the Board of Survey regarding the report?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: They are not responsible for the contents of the report.
They are jointly responsible for the accuracy of the report.
Only the Chairman is responsible for the report's accuracy.
They are only responsible for the physical counting.

explanation: The fact that the report must be signed by all members implies that they are jointly responsible for its accuracy.

text: What is the implication of the Board of Survey's findings for an officer-in-charge?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The findings have no consequences for the officer.
The officer is solely responsible for any discrepancies.
The officer is immediately dismissed if a shortage is found.
The officer's responsibility is discharged only after a satisfactory report is submitted.

explanation: The officer-in-charge must be present during the count and the Board's report is submitted for investigation of discrepancies, which implies the officer is responsible for the items under their charge. Part 3: Financial Regulations book: Pension Scheme in the Federal Public Service

text: What is the primary purpose of Chapter 19 of the Financial Regulations book?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To define the roles of Accounting Officers.
To outline the pension scheme in the Federal Public Service.
To detail procedures for internal audit.

explanation: Chapter 19 is titled "Pension Scheme in the Federal Public Service.”

text: According to Financial Regulation 1904(a), who is responsible for opening Retirement Savings Accounts (RSA) for each employee?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 1904(a) states that the National Pension Commission (NPC) will open Retirement Savings Accounts (RSA) for each employee.

text: What is one of the responsibilities of the National Pension Commission regarding accounting records?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To destroy accounting records after five years.
To maintain accounting records for contributions and ensure proper periodic reconciliation.
To delegate all accounting responsibilities to ministries.
To only report to the Auditor-General.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1904(c) states that the Commission shall maintain accounting records for the contributions and ensure proper periodic reconciliation of the accounts.

text: How often should the National Pension Commission generate and distribute Retirement Savings Account (RSA) statements to contributing employees?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 1904(d) mandates that on a quarterly basis, the commission shall generate and distribute Retirement Savings Account (RSA) statements to each contributing employee.

text: What rank must a liaison officer designated by each ministry or agency for pension matters not be below?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 1904(e) specifies that each ministry or agency shall designate a liaison officer not below the rank of a Director. 282

text: How should the Subsidiary Account Pension Unit function in relation to the main subsidiary accounts section of ministries?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: It should be integrated with the main section.
It should report directly to the Accountant-General.
It should be supervised by the main accounts section.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1905 states that the section shall function independently of the main subsidiary accounts section.

text: Who allocates a Below-the-Line Classification code for the recording of monthly pension contributions?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Director of Finance and Accounts.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1906 states that the Accountant-General shall allocate a Below-the-Line Classification code.

text: On receipt of monthly personnel cost warrants, what should the Director of Finance and Accounts ensure is issued?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: A payment advice to the Central Bank of Nigeria.
A Treasury Receipt Book 6 in respect of the gross amount on the warrant.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1907 states that on receipt of monthly personnel cost warrants, the Director of Finance and Accounts shall ensure the issuance of Treasury Receipt Book 6. 283

text: What is the overall goal of the pension scheme outlined in Chapter 19?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To ensure proper administration and accounting of pension contributions.
To provide short-term loans to employees.

explanation: The chapter details the administration, responsibilities of various entities, and accounting procedures for the pension scheme, indicating its goal is proper management of contributions.

text: What document provides the legal framework for the investment of pension funds by the Central Bank of Nigeria?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 1904(b) states that investments are made "as provided in the Pension Reform Act.”

text: What is a "Below-the-Line Classification code" used for in the context of pension contributions?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 1906 states that this code is used "for the recording of monthly pension contributions.” 284

text: Who issues the monthly personnel cost warrants that trigger the pension accounting procedures?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Director of Finance and Accounts.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1907 indicates that the Director of Finance and Accounts receives "monthly personnel cost warrants from the Budget Office.”

text: What type of account is the Retirement Savings Account (RSA)?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: An account specific to each employee for pension contributions.
A suspense account for unclaimed funds.
An investment account managed by ministries.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1904(a) states the NPC will open “Retirement Savings Accounts (RSA) for each employee.”

text: What aspect of contributions does the National Pension Commission credit to the Retirement Savings Accounts (RSA)?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Both employer and employee contributions, and interest earned.

explanation: Financial Regulation 1904(a) specifies that the NPC will credit "both the collections and interest earned to the account.”

text: What fundamental principle of financial management is supported by the detailed accounting procedures for pensions in Chapter 197
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Transparency and accountability in public finance.

explanation: The detailed regulations, reconciliation requirements, and independent unit creation all support principles of transparency and accountability in managing pension funds. Part 4: Financial Regulation: Government Vehicles

text: What is the primary purpose of government vehicles, as stated in Financial Regulation 2001?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: For personal use by government officials.
For official duties of the government.

explanation: Financial Regulation 2001 states that government vehicles are provided for official duties of the government.

text: Who is held personally responsible for the efficient and economical use of government vehicles within their Ministry, Extra-Ministerial Office, or other arm of government?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 2002 states that the Accounting Officer is personally responsible for the efficient and economical use of government vehicles. 286

text: What information must be clearly displayed on the front and rear number plates of all government vehicles?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The official registration number and the inscription “Federal Government" or “State Government.”

explanation: Financial Regulation 2004 requires that all government vehicles must display the official registration number and the inscription “Federal Government" or "State Government” on both front and rear number plates.

text: Which document must be carried in every government vehicle, and why?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Vehicle purchase invoice for proof of ownership.
The logbook (Treasury Form 141) for recording journey details.
The vehicle service history for maintenance records.
The driver's medical certificate for emergencies.

explanation: Financial Regulation 2005 mandates that a logbook (Treasury Form 141) must be carried in every vehicle for recording details of journeys.

text: Who i responsible for ensuring the proper and up-to-date maintenance of the logbook?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 2005 states that the driver is responsible for the proper and up-to-date maintenance of the logbook. 287

text: Who is responsible for examining the logbook regularly and signing against the entries?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: The Permanent Secretary or Head of Extra-Ministerial Office.

explanation: Financial Regulation 2007 states that the Permanent Secretary or Head of Extra-Ministerial Office shall examine the logbook regularly and sign against the entries.

text: What is the frequency for the Mechanical Engineer to verify and certify the fuel and lubricants consumption?
subject: Financial Regulations
explanation: Financial Regulation 2008 requires the Mechanical Engineer to verify and certify fuel and lubricants consumption monthly.

text: What action must be taken for all journeys outside office hours or during weekends and public holidays?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: They require the written permission of the Accounting Officer or his delegated representative.
They are permitted for personal use.
They must be reported to the police.

explanation: Financial Regulation 2009 states that journeys outside office hours, weekends, and public holidays require the written permission of the Accounting Officer or his delegated representative.

text: What action should be taken by the Head of Division or Unit when a government vehicle is involved in an accident?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: Ignore it if there is no major damage.
Report it immediately to the Accounting Officer.
Take the vehicle for repairs without reporting.
Attempt to resolve the matter privately.

explanation: Financial Regulation 2011 requires the Head of Division or Unit to report vehicle accidents immediately to the Accounting Officer.

text: What document must the Accounting Officer ensure is filled out immediately after a government vehicle accident?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: An accident claim form from the insurance company.
A Report of Loss of Government Funds or Stores (Treasury Form 146). C/ A police incident report.

explanation: Financial Regulation 2012 requires the Accounting Officer to ensure that a Report of Loss of Government Funds or Stores (Treasury Form 146) is filled out immediately.

text: What is the role of the Mechanical Engineer after a government vehicle accident?
subject: Financial Regulations

options.text: To inspect the vehicle and prepare an estimate of the cost of repairs.
